items.name: unslop
items.description: A Claude skill that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface

readme.excerpt:
Created by Damir Sokolovsky (@heydamir), who started the Unslopping series on X.

unslop is a skill for Claude Code and Codex that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

Passes. Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
Visuals. Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service l

items.name: doory
items.description: Open source canva alternative

readme.excerpt:
Doory is a design editor that runs in the browser: posters, social posts, stories, slides, invitations, resumes, thumbnails and business cards. You start from a template or a blank page, edit everything on it, and export PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF, MP4 or GIF. There is no paid plan, you don't need an account to start, and you can run it on your own server with Docker or without it.

It is a young project: the editor is complete, the template library is small (ten starter templates), and bug reports are very welcome.

Editing. Tools sit in a rail on the left and open as panels; the toolbar above the page changes with what you select. Animation. Enter, exit and emphasis animations, page transitions, music and sound effects. Present it, or export it as a video or GIF. Layers. Rename, lock, hide, group and reorder anything, or right-click it to copy, duplicate and arrange. Share and export. One menu for share links, downloads and presenting. Downloads are made in the browser; print PDFs can have bleed and crop marks.

items.name: beszel
items.description: Lightweight server monitoring with historical data, docker stats, and alerts.

readme.excerpt:
Beszel is a lightweight server monitoring platform that includes Docker statistics, historical data, and alert functions.

It has a friendly web interface, simple configuration, and is ready to use out of the box. It supports automatic backup, multi-user, OAuth authentication, and API access.

- Lightweight : Smaller and less resource-intensive than leading solutions. - Simple : Easy setup with little manual configuration required. - Alerts : Configurable alerts for most metrics. Supports many notification services. - Docker stats : Tracks CPU, memory, and network usage history for each container. - Network monitoring : Monitor response time and interruptions directly from agents. - S.M.A.R.T. : Disk health data and notifications on drive failure. - Multi-user : Users manage their own systems. Admins can share systems across users. - OAuth / OIDC : Supports many OAuth2 providers. Password auth can be disabled. - Automatic backups : Save to and restore from disk or S3-compatible storage.

readme.excerpt:
244 pixel art effects and animations, every one a small piece of code. Fire, explosions, magic, weather, UI, pickups, critters and more. Play them live, recolor and mirror them, drop them into a browser game, or export sprite sheets for any engine. Plus a Claude Code skill that makes new ones the way a picky pixel artist would: draft, render, look, refine.

Every effect that involves a character is acted out : he winds up, lets go, freezes on contact and recovers, and a target takes the hit. Twelve whole moves chain the effects into attacks from wind-up to recovery.

open the gallery · catalog · acting · the skill · make your own · how it works
features: "Add a frost nova to my mage's ultimate."
"Make five takes on a coin pickup sparkle and show me the best two."
"Export the fire and explosions categories as sprite sheets for Godot."
"This hit effect feels floaty. Make it punchier."
"Give this spell a wind-up and make the enemy react to it."
Two kinds of effect, no images. Pure effects export draw(p, t, o) , the frame at t seconds from t alone, so
Two buffers. color takes pixels: opaque, dithered or truly translucent. light takes additive glow, added on
Seeded everything. Every random number comes from the effect's seed, so frame 40 is the same every time.

items.name: Orkas
items.description: Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first AI team for your desktop: a Commander turns your goal into to-dos and coordinates 16 built-in specialist agents plus Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes, with projects, scheduled automations and connectors. Free app for macOS & Windows; built-in models or your own keys.

readme.excerpt:
An open-source team of AI agents on your desktop — it turns your goals into finished work and keeps it moving.

Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app — an AI assistant that works as a team. Tell the Commander what you need: it finishes many tasks on its own, and for bigger work it plans the steps and brings in specialist agents along with the coding and personal agents you already use — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent — to work on it together.

Orkas is built to keep a project moving, not just answer one prompt. A project holds the goal, rules, memory and files, so every new conversation picks up where the last one left off. To-dos split the work between people and agents, Auto-advance lets the team take on the next to-do by itself, and scheduled automations repeat routine work hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. All your data stays on your computer, and finished work comes back for your review — so you can trust Orkas with the ongoing work of your business.
